subject: Pegasus Systems — latency & throughput qualification run plan
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Cho <alex.cho@pegasus.ai>, Priya Nair <priya.nair@pegasus.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pegasus — post-demo recap & proposed A/B bench plan

Team — quick recap from this morning's call with Pegasus (Alex/Priya). They ran a short POC with a hyperscaler endpoint and saw ~18% higher p95 latency vs their on-prem baseline at ~2k tokens/sec, and want a focused qualification to understand the delta across real customer prompts.

Key asks from Pegasus:
- Confirm a repeatable A/B plan that compares Redwood-hosted inference vs the hyperscaler they tested (us-east region).
- Measure p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and tail latency under two workload shapes: short chat (avg 60 tokens, bursty) and long-form summarization (avg 1,200 tokens, streaming).
- Prefer 95th/99th latency breakdowns by model variant (fp16 vs 4-bit quant) and by batching policy.

My suggested scope (attached: pegasus_bench_spec_v1.xlsx):
- 2 test scenarios (chat, long-form), 3 model variants (open-v1, open-v1-q4, redwood-small-q4), 3 concurrency points (low=2, med=8, high=32) — run each for 30 minutes to stabilize p95.
- Collect token/sec (steady-state), p50/p95/p99, 95th tail by request size buckets, and error rates.
- Use our probe script (measure_tokens_per_sec.sh) with KV-cache warmup and identical prompt sets (Pegasus will share).

Open items for engineering help:
- Marcus: confirm the probe script (I attached draft) and whether 30m windows are sufficient to capture autoscaler behavior.
- Marcus/Jordan: what additional telemetry would you want in the CSV exports to help the customer side-by-side (traces, token counts, batch sizes, kernel timings)?

Next steps / timeline:
- Today: confirm test matrix and telemetry items (internal).
- Mon 3/12: run dry-run in staging (redwood-staging-us-east).
- Wed 3/14: run customer-facing A/B with Pegasus present for first 30 minutes.

Alex/Priya — thanks for the time. We want to make these runs reproducible so Pegasus can validate. Please confirm you can provide the sample prompts and preferred windows (we proposed Wed 3/14 10–13 PT).

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Attachment: pegasus_bench_spec_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Cho <alex.cho@pegasus.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Mar 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pegasus — post-demo recap & proposed A/B bench plan

All — quick technical notes after skimming the spec and the sample numbers Alex shared on the call:

1) Measurement methodology:
- Use controlled clients that replay the exact prompt set with deterministic seeds. We should run KV-cache warmup passes equal to 5x median sequence length for long-form to avoid cold-cache noise.
- For tokens/sec, measure both "observed throughput" (tokens emitted per second) and "server-side tokens/sec" (from runtime accounting) to catch tokenization differences.

2) Latency windows and statistical confidence:
- 30m windows are OK for low/med concurrency. For high=32 we should extend to 45m to observe autoscaler step-down behavior and p99 stability.

3) Telemetry we should export in CSV: timestamp, request_id, model_variant, sequence_length, batch_size, batch_latency_ms, kernel_exec_ms, gpu_util_pct, tokens_emitted, kv_cache_hit, region, instance_type.

4) Suggested test harness updates (attached: measure_tokens_per_sec.sh) — it now logs per-request token counts and optionally toggles batching policies (immediate, 10ms delay, 50ms delay).

I'll stand up a staging run template on redwood-staging and ping when ready.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Attachment: measure_tokens_per_sec.sh (bash script)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Nair <priya.nair@pegasus.ai>, procurement@pegasus.ai
Date: Fri, 09 Mar 2028 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pegasus — post-demo recap & proposed A/B bench plan

Hannah/Marcus — good plan. A couple of commercial notes to thread into the schedule:
- Pegasus asked for an apples-to-apples cost estimate for the two runs (hyperscaler vs Redwood-hosted) including expected unit costs at the three concurrency points. We should prepare a short "delta sheet" they can take to procurement.
- They mentioned a possible preference for a short dedicated pool for the customer-facing run if we show consistent tail improvements — please outline what a 2-week dedicated trial would look like (cost, SLA, ingress limits).

Proposed timeline tweak: run our staging dry-run Monday morning (3/12), and schedule the customer-facing A/B for Wed 3/14 11:00–14:00 PT to capture their east-coast ops. If Pegasus can confirm 11:00, we can get an internal exec on the call for the first 30 minutes.

I'll draft the delta sheet after Marcus confirms telemetry and expected GPU hours per run.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.ai

From: Alex Cho <alex.cho@pegasus.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Nair <priya.nair@pegasus.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Mar 2028 16:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pegasus — post-demo recap & proposed A/B bench plan

Thanks for the clear plan — we can do Wed 3/14 11:00–14:00 PT. Priya from procurement is on copy; procurement@pegasus.ai will expect the cost delta.

Quick clarifications from our side:
- Prompt sets: we'll upload two archives to your Drive link by EOD Monday (chat_prompts.zip, longform_prompts.zip).
- Preferred model variants to test on our hyperscaler baseline: open-v1 (fp16) and open-v1-q4 (their current cached variant). For Redwood, please include your redwood-small-q4 and the open-v1-q4 equivalent.
- For long-form streaming, please ensure the probe emits 1 token at a time to simulate streaming latency (we want to see end-to-end time-to-first-token and time-to-last-token).

We appreciate the 45m suggestion for the high concurrency run — let's extend only the high=32 run to 45m.

See you Wed.

Alex Cho
Senior ML Engineer, Pegasus Systems
alex.cho@pegasus.ai
